scenario: A trade circular highlights only vineyard labels that survive export expansion and maintain gross margin above 25%. Merchants use the highlighted average margin to infer typical margin across all labels.

data.description: Only surviving labels with margin above 25% are highlighted. Margin is Normal with sigma 7 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean gross margin mu across all labels and (b) the fraction of labels highlighted.
naive_answer: Typical gross margin is about 28.7% because that is the circular average.
naive_trap: Only upper-tail surviving labels are shown.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.0.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(25-mu)/7; return mu+7*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-28.68
mu=brentq(eq,-50,24.99)
frac=norm.sf((25-mu)/7)
assert abs(mu-18)<0.5 and abs(frac-0.1587)<0.005
